messages:
jun: Quick follow-up to the attention/quant RFC — should we add a thin kernel-adapter layer that handles dequant+gemm fusion for mixed FP8/INT8/INT4 paths at the runtime boundary?

maria: short answer: yes if we can keep it opt-in and low-overhead. fusion buys a lot on throughput but can complicate scheduling. :thinking_face:

alex: agree with maria. my concern is the ABI surface. if every model can register a bespoke fused kernel we need a stable registration API and versioning.

liam: perf note from my microbench on A100: naive dequant -> GEMM -> quant path is ~1.9x slower than a fused dequant+matmul for INT8->FP32 accumulation. FP8 fusion showed ~2.5x on short sequences. numbers vary with seq len.

jun: thanks. proposal: runtime exposes a small adapter interface so kernels can opt into doing dequant+matmul in one call. fallback remains to generic path. something like: 

alex: example ABI sketch: 

```c
// simplified prototype for kernel registration
typedef enum {QFMT_FP8, QFMT_INT8, QFMT_INT4} qfmt_t;
typedef int (*kernel_fn_t)(const void* qweights, const void* qinput, void* output, size_t n, void* ctx);
int register_quant_kernel(const char* name, qfmt_t w_fmt, qfmt_t i_fmt, kernel_fn_t fn, const char* hw_tags);
```

maria: that's a good start. we should include metadata for kv-cache layout expectations and whether kernel preserves packed layout. otherwise routing/batching will break.

jun: right — think we need kernel_meta flags: preserves_kv_layout, supports_prefix_cache, max_sequence, requires_aligned_stride. would be in the meta param.

tara: another gotcha: memory blowup when we materialize dequanted weights for many models. if fused kernels can work directly on quantized weights (keep them on GPU), we avoid extra copies. so adapter must allow both in-place and materialize modes.

liam: +1. also need a per-request flag to opt-out for correctness/regression testing. i.e., runtime should support forcing generic dequant path for debugging.

alex: session-level negotiation idea: at model load time runtime selects the best kernel based on model fmt, hw_tags, runtime heuristics (seq distribution) and registers a chosen kernel instance for that model id. if capacity is low or kernel fails, we auto-fallback to generic path.

jun: does anyone worry about the explosion of kernel binaries? we could provide a small set of canonical fused kernels (FP8->FP32 acc, INT8->FP32, INT4->FP16) and vendors can add optimized variants via hw_tags. runtime picks most specific match.

maria: yes but we should cap kernel variants per hw_tag to avoid scheduling chaos. maybe a ranking score: perf_score - memory_penalty - frag_penalty. runtime picks top K.

tara: KV cache interaction: fused kernels must expose hooks for incremental kv append and read so we can batch across requests. if kernel hides its KV layout, batching engine cannot merge requests. need a small KV descriptor in the ABI.

alex: sketch for KV descriptor: 
```c
struct kv_desc { size_t elem_size; size_t stride; bool interleaved; bool requires_transpose; };
int kernel_supports_kv(const char* kernel_name, const kv_desc* out);
```

liam: can we keep correctness testing cheap? propose adding a lightweight fast-check that compares fused kernel outputs vs generic path on ~50 random prompts during rollout canary. if mismatch > epsilon, mark kernel unhealthy.

maria: operationally, rollout should be gradual: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback if regression detected. console can show per-kernel error rates.

jun: sounds like we have consensus on adapter+meta+kv-desc+canary. open questions: support for INT4 packing schemes (nibbles) — should adapter hide packing/unpacking?

alex: best if kernel receives quantized packed buffers and knows how to decode. adapter shouldn't unpack globally because that defeats perf. adapter can provide small helpers for common packing.

tara: note on memory: INT4 unpacked to FP16 doubles memory. in our Dedicated mode with many concurrent models that is non-starter. we must prefer direct-packed fused kernels.

jun: actionable items: 1) Alex to draft kernel-adapter API PR (include meta, kv-desc, hw_tags). 2) Liam to run microbench suite for FP8/INT8/INT4 fused vs generic across seq lens. 3) Maria to add rollout/canary plan for console integration. 4) Tara to list KV layout patterns we need to support.

alex: I can drop a PR by EOD tomorrow. will include the C ABI sketch + python bindings for registration.

liam: I'll add benchmarks to infra-bench and push numbers as a short doc.

maria: I'll stub console metrics and promote a telemetry event: kernel_fusion_decision{model, kernel, perf_delta}.

build-bot: CI pipeline: branch alex/quant-adapter created. Running unit tests.

jun: great. thanks everyone. we'll use this thread as the design log. if anyone wants to push back on the ABI or flags, reply here and I'll fold into the PR. :rocket:
